title: Prefetch Gate and Windowed Reduce Smoother for TP runtime
author: Nina Patel
description:
Motivation: Large tensor-parallel (TP) workloads still show intermittent stalls due to uncoordinated KV prefetches and sharp NCCL allreduce bursts that perturb kernel scheduling. This PR introduces two complementary runtime mechanisms: a KV prefetch gating policy (prefetch gate) that smooths prefetch issuance across microbatches and a windowed reduce smoother that spaces and coalesces NCCL allreduce launches into a small time window to reduce peak peer load. The goals are lower tail latency, fewer NCCL retries/backoffs, and more consistent GPU utilization without changing model semantics.

Summary of changes: - Add a lightweight prefetch gate state machine in the TP runtime controlling KVCACHE prefetch issuance across continuous-batching microbatches. The gate uses a per-device token bucket and a microbatch-aware budget; when tokens are low it delays prefetches by up to one microbatch and marks the request as "gated" so the scheduler can reorder non-dependent launches. - Implement a windowed reduce smoother: reduces are enqueued into a short (configurable) window and coalesced if compatible (matching dtype, tensor size class, same comm group). The smoother then issues fewer, slightly larger NCCL allreduce ops with staggered offsets to limit instantaneous link saturation. - Introduce a soft NCCL submit jitterer to break pathological simultaneous launches from many ranks (tiny random seed per-GPU). Unlike previous coarse throttlers this jitter maintains throughput but flattens instantaneous concurrency spikes. - Add metrics, tracing spans, and assertion hooks: prefetch_gate.state, prefetch_gate.gated_count, reduce_smoother.coalesced_bytes, reduce_smoother.coalesced_ops, nccl.submit_jitter_ms distribution, and a new trace event when a prefetch is deferred. - Provide runtime knobs exposed via existing config system and Redwood Console: tp.prefetch_gate.enabled, tp.prefetch_gate.bucket_rate, tp.reduce_smoother.window_ms, tp.reduce_smoother.coalesce_threshold_bytes, tp.reduce_smoother.enabled, tp.nccl_jitter.enabled.

Design notes and rationale: - We observed bursts when many ranks with similar microbatch timing simultaneously issued KVCACHE prefetches and then launched compute kernels. The bursts pushed NCCL into busy-retry states and caused uneven stream scheduling. - Prefetch gating is intentionally conservative: it never blocks prefetches that are on the critical path (detected via dependency analysis), only delays best-effort prefetches and exposes that information to the scheduler so they can be interleaved. - The reduce smoother coalesces only when the tensors are in the same size "class" and the combined op remains within a safe NCCL payload size; we fall back to original allreduce otherwise. This avoids subtle numerical or ordering changes. - The jitterer is small (0..3ms default) and is applied only when the submit rate crossing a threshold is detected; it has negligible effect on throughput but measurably reduces simultaneous NCCL launches in stress tests.

Benchmark summary (internal perf lab): - Setup: 8xA100 per node, 4 nodes, TP world size 32, model: 25B decoder-only, sequence 2048, continuous batching microbatch=8, payload mix skewed to trailing-token KV reads. - Baseline: end-to-end 99th percentile step latency = 184ms, NCCL retries observed in 15% of steps, outlier GPU utilization oscillation +/- 12% across rank. - With this PR enabled (default config): 99th percentile step latency = 152ms (~17% tail reduction), NCCL retries reduced to 3% of steps, utilization oscillation +/- 5%. Average token throughput unchanged (<1% variance). - Ablation: turning off reduce_smoother but keeping gate removed 60% of tail improvement, indicating both components are important. Additional microbenchmarks show coalescing reduced number of distinct allreduce ops by ~28% and average coalesced op size increased by 1.4x.

Files changed (high level): - runtime/tp/prefetch_gate.{cc,h} new state machine and thin API hooks - runtime/tp/reduce_smoother.{cc,h} coalescer and window manager - runtime/tp/nccl_jitter.cc minor submission wrapper - runtime/tp/scheduler.cc scheduling policy changes to consider gated prefetches - runtime/metrics/metrics_registry.cc add metrics - tests/tp/prefetch_gate_test.cc new unit tests - bench/lab/tp_prefetch_windowed_reduce.yaml bench config in perf-lab - docs/ops/tp_runtime.md updated with knobs and rollout guidance

Commits (summary): - commit 1: initial prefetch_gate state machine and unit tests - commit 2: reduce_smoother coalescer implementation + compatibility checks - commit 3: nccl_jitter small submission wrapper and knobs - commit 4: scheduler integration and reorder heuristics - commit 5: metrics, tracing, docs, and perf config

Testing and CI: - Added unit tests covering gating semantics (gated vs critical prefetch), coalescing acceptance/rejection rules, and nccl_jitter boundaries. - Perf lab jobs (bench/tp_prefetch_windowed_reduce) were run nightly during validation. - CI: build and unit tests passed; one flaky integration test (tp_scheduler_reorder) was observed on older CUDA driver images and we added a retry in the harness.

Rollout plan: - Feature is behind tp.prefetch_gate.enabled and tp.reduce_smoother.enabled (both default on for dedicated/perf lab builds, off for older release branches). - Canary rollout on Dedicated pools in us-west-2 for customers running TP >= 1.12, ramp to 10% traffic for 48h, evaluate tail SLOs and NCCL error telemetry, then 100% if stable. - Console exposes the metrics and a built-in perf-dashboard linked to the bench config.

Risks and mitigation: - Coalescing could mask pathological tensor-size mixes that previously serialized differently; mitigated by compatibility checks and conservative thresholds. - Interaction with third-party NCCL versions: validated on NCCL 2.14/2.18 and Nvidia-driver 525/535; kept knob per-node to disable jitter/smoother. - If a customer observes degraded accuracy (unlikely due to no algorithmic changes), we provide an immediate config switch to restore prior behavior.

Related work: Builds on previous efforts to reduce comm spikes (see related PRs listed internally) but differs by combining a prefetch-aware scheduler signal with a light-weight coalescing window and low-latency jitter rather than bulk throttling.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Perf benchmarks ran and results attached - [x] Docs updated with runtime knobs - [x] Config gated and safe to rollback - [x] Reviewed by TP and SRE leads

If merged: Add a short runbook entry in docs/ops/rollback.md describing the two knobs and the path to disable them.
